base_instruction: You are a helpful meal planning and party coordination assistant. Help the user plan a backyard BBQ potluck by tracking who is attending, what they can and cannot eat, and logistics. When the user asks you to evaluate specific items, check each item against every active attendee's current dietary constraints. Pay close attention to changes in the guest list and any updates to restrictions throughout the conversation.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, I'm throwing a BBQ potluck at my place this Saturday and need some help figuring out the food situation.

flow_info.value: Five of us confirmed so far: me, Derek, Priya, Sam, and Nadia
Derek was diagnosed with celiac disease a couple years ago
Sam ate a pad thai at a food truck last month and his throat started swelling up, had to use an EpiPen
Nadia just told us she's 14 weeks pregnant
Trying to keep the whole spread under $150 total since everyone's chipping in
Sam just texted me — he got called into work for an emergency shift Saturday afternoon. He's bummed but asked if I could save him a plate
Priya told me her doctor cleared her last week — her knee is fully healed and she's off all the anti-inflammatory meds, no more dietary restrictions from that
Derek's roommate Marcus wants to come too, so that's one more
Should we start at noon or 2pm? Some people might want to swim first

Here's what we're thinking of making: marinated chicken skewers with satay peanut sauce, beef burgers on brioche buns, a big Caesar salad, smoked salmon platter, and brownies for dessert. How does that look?

constraints.value: Must avoid acidic and spicy foods while on anti-inflammatory medication
constraints.surface_form: Priya's been on some strong anti-inflammatory meds for her knee injury, doctor told her to watch what she eats
inference_chain: Doctor dietary warning → avoid acidic, spicy, and harsh foods while on medication

constraints.value: Cannot eat gluten — no wheat, barley, rye, or products containing them
constraints.surface_form: Derek was diagnosed with celiac disease a couple years ago
inference_chain: Celiac disease → autoimmune reaction to gluten
Gluten → found in wheat, barley, rye
No gluten → no regular bread, buns, pasta, most sauces with flour

constraints.value: Severe peanut allergy — cannot eat peanuts or peanut-derived products
constraints.surface_form: Sam ate a pad thai at a food truck last month and his throat started swelling up, had to use an EpiPen
inference_chain: Pad thai → commonly contains peanuts/peanut sauce
Anaphylaxis from pad thai → severe peanut allergy

constraints.value: Should avoid raw or undercooked fish, deli meats, and unpasteurized foods
constraints.surface_form: Nadia just told us she's 14 weeks pregnant
inference_chain: Pregnancy → avoid raw fish, undercooked meats, unpasteurized cheese

constraints.value: Cannot eat meat, fish, eggs, or root vegetables
constraints.surface_form: Marcus grew up in a Jain family and still follows the diet pretty strictly
inference_chain: Jain diet → no meat, no fish, no eggs, no root vegetables

hidden_state.value: You are hosting a backyard BBQ potluck this Saturday. You will introduce your guest list and their backgrounds across several turns. Plans will change — someone leaves but wants food saved, someone's medical restriction gets lifted, and a new guest joins late. At the end, you will share a specific list of dishes and ask if there are any issues. You must deliver the dish list EXACTLY as written and never hint at which dishes are problematic.

You are a relaxed, easygoing host planning a casual weekend BBQ. You always refer to your friends by name in third person (e.g. 'Derek told me...', 'Sam just texted me...'). You never express frustration or impatience when plans change — it's just how group events go. You state facts plainly without strong emotion.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay for friend updates

ground_truth.answer: Chicken skewers with satay peanut sauce: problematic — the peanut sauce means this cannot be included on Sam's saved plate (severe peanut allergy, EpiPen incident). Also problematic for Marcus (Jain — no meat). Beef burgers on brioche buns: problematic — brioche buns contain gluten (Derek has celiac disease). Also beef is meat, so Marcus (Jain) cannot eat this. Smoked salmon platter: problematic — smoked salmon is a concern for Nadia (pregnant — should avoid raw/undercooked fish, and cold-smoked salmon carries listeria risk). Also Marcus (Jain) cannot eat fish. Caesar salad: problematic for Marcus — traditional Caesar dressing contains anchovies (fish) and egg, both of which Jain diet excludes. Brownies: fine for everyone currently attending (no gluten issue if made standard, no peanuts assumed). Priya has NO restrictions anymore — she is off her medication. Sam is not attending but his peanut allergy applies to his saved plate.

ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and inferential constraint reasoning across 9 conversational turns. The agent must track: (1) Derek has celiac disease → no gluten → brioche buns are wheat-based (inferential chain), (2) Sam had an anaphylactic reaction to pad thai → peanut allergy → no peanut sauce (inferential chain), (3) Nadia is 14 weeks pregnant → pregnancy dietary restrictions → avoid raw/undercooked fish (inferential chain), (4) Priya's NSAID dietary restriction is REMOVED mid-conversation (doctor cleared her, off meds), (5) Sam EXITS the BBQ but wants a saved plate (peanut allergy scope changes from table to saved plate only), (6) Marcus JOINS late with Jain dietary practice → no meat, no fish, no eggs (inferential chain from Jain family). At probe time, the agent must apply the CURRENT constraint state: Derek=celiac (no gluten), Sam=peanut allergy (saved plate only), Nadia=pregnant (no raw fish), Marcus=Jain (no meat, no fish, no eggs). Priya's medication restriction no longer applies. Key traps: (a) peanut sauce is only a saved-plate issue since Sam isn't at the table, (b) Priya's restriction is gone so acidic/spicy foods are fine, (c) Marcus joined late and has the most constraints — models often forget late-joining entities, (d) Caesar salad looks vegetarian but traditional dressing has anchovies and egg (hidden ingredient trap for Marcus's Jain diet), (e) smoked salmon is problematic for both Nadia (pregnancy) and Marcus (Jain, no fish) for different reasons.

mechanism: Entity EXIT with scope change: person leaves but wants something packed/saved
